extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of electric utilities and independent power producers, facility environmental/compliance managers, qualified professional engineers, state regulators, and EPA staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for identifying CCR management units and for the design, monitoring, inspection, reporting, and closure/post-closure activities of CCR units (including timelines and certification requirements). Targets owners/operators, qualified professional engineers, and state/EPA reviewers responsible for compliance with 40 CFR part 257 subpart D amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inactive CCR surface impoundment (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means a CCR surface impoundment located at an active facility that no longer receives CCR on or after October 19, 2015, and still contains both CCR and liquids on or after October 19, 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inactive facility / inactive electric utility or independent power producer (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means any electric utility or independent power producer that ceased providing power to electric power transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems before October 19, 2015. An off-site disposal facility is inactive if it ceased accepting or managing CCR prior to October 19, 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infiltration (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means the migration or movement of liquid, such as surface water or ground water, into or through a CCR unit from any direction, including from the surface, laterally, and through the bottom of the unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy CCR surface impoundment (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means a CCR surface impoundment that no longer receives CCR but contained both CCR and liquids on or after October 19, 2015, and that is located at an inactive electric utility or independent power producer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquids (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means any fluid (such as water) that has no independent shape but has a definite volume and does not expand indefinitely and that is only slightly compressible; encompasses water sluiced into impoundment, precipitation, surface water, groundwater, and any water migrated into the impoundment, found as free water or porewater intermingled with CCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means the person(s) responsible for the overall operation of a CCR unit, including those responsible for disposal or otherwise actively engaged in solid waste management of CCR and those directing or overseeing groundwater monitoring, closure or post-closure activities at a CCR unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means the person(s) who owns a CCR unit or part of a CCR unit, or a facility, whether in full or in part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulated CCR unit (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means any new CCR landfill, existing CCR landfill, new CCR surface impoundment, existing CCR surface impoundment, inactive CCR surface impoundment, or legacy CCR surface impoundment; does not include CCR management units.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Director (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means the chief administrative officer of the lead state agency responsible for implementing the state program regulating disposal in CCR units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technically feasible / feasible (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means possible to do in a way that would likely be successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technically infeasible / infeasible (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: means not possible to do in a way that would likely be successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wetlands location restriction (§257.61)
rubrics_metrics.description: New CCR landfills, existing and new CCR surface impoundments, and all lateral expansions of CCR units must not be located in wetlands (as defined), unless the owner or operator demonstrates by specified dates that the CCR unit meets the requirements of paragraphs (a)(1) through (5) of §257.61.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner/operator may locate in wetlands only upon meeting the enumerated demonstration requirements by the deadlines in paragraph (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural integrity applicability (§257.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of paragraphs (a)(1) through (4) of §257.73 apply to all existing CCR surface impoundments and legacy CCR surface impoundments, except for those that are incised CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing and legacy impoundments (except incised) must meet structural integrity criteria specified in §257.73.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of CCR management unit identification requirements (§257.75(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of §257.75 apply to owners and operators of active facilities or facilities with a legacy CCR surface impoundment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility evaluation to identify CCR management units (§257.75(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner or operator of an active facility or a facility with a legacy CCR surface impoundment must conduct a facility evaluation to identify all CCR management units at the facility via thorough evaluation of reasonably and readily available records and a physical inspection; where necessary physical inspection must include field investigation activities (exploratory soil borings, geophysical assessments, etc.) to fill data gaps and establish location/boundaries of potential CCR management units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facility evaluation must identify all CCR management units regardless of when they came into existence; physical inspection used to affirmatively rule out potential CCR placement areas identified during records review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility Evaluation Report Part 1 content and certifications (§257.75(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: By no later than Feb 9, 2026 prepare Facility Evaluation Report Part 1 containing, to the extent reasonably and readily available, items (i) through (xiv) including owner/operator identity and unit IDs, maps/topo location, purposes of units, foundation/abutment descriptions, records of spills/releases, structural instability records, groundwater contamination records, size/volume estimates, dates CCR first/ceased receiving, CCR types, narratives of closure activities, documentation reviewed, supporting information used to identify/evaluate units, and narrative of data gaps and plan to remedy them with milestones and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 1 must be certified by a qualified professional engineer that it meets paragraph (c)(1) requirements; owner/operator must sign a penalty-of-law certification statement attesting to truth/accuracy/completeness; place report in facility operating record per §257.105(f)(25); notify EPA of establishment of CCR website as required; if no CCR management units exist, submit Part 1 documenting steps taken to determine absence and include certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility Evaluation Report Part 2 content and certifications (§257.75(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: By no later than Feb 8, 2027 prepare Facility Evaluation Report Part 2 containing, to the extent not provided in Part 1, items (i) through (xiii) obtained from a physical evaluation (including field sampling as necessary): similar identification items, location, purposes, foundation descriptions, further evidence of spills/releases, instability, groundwater contamination, unit size, CCR types, closure activities narrative, nature/extent of field oversight and data reviewed, additional supporting information, explanation how data gaps from Part 1 were addressed, and documentation for any deferral under §257.101(g) or (h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 2 must be certified by a qualified professional engineer; owner/operator must sign the penalty-of-law certification; place Part 2 in facility operating record per §257.105(f)(26); if no CCR management units exist, submit Part 2 documenting steps taken to determine absence and include certifications; updates to Part 1 data gap remedy plan must be added to the record during Part 2 timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping, notification, and internet compliance for facility evaluation (§257.75(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or operator of the facility must comply with the recordkeeping requirements in §257.105(f), the notification requirements in §257.106(f), and the internet requirements in §257.107(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Air criteria to minimize airborne CCR (§257.80(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or operator of a CCR unit must adopt measures that will effectively minimize CCR from becoming airborne at the facility, including CCR fugitive dust originating from CCR units, roads, and other CCR management and material handling activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR fugitive dust control plan amendment (§257.80(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator may amend the written CCR fugitive dust control plan at any time provided the revised plan is placed in the facility's operating record as required by §257.105(g)(1); must amend the written plan no later than 30 days whenever there is a change in conditions that would substantially affect the written plan in effect (e.g., construction and operation of a new CCR unit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydrologic and hydraulic capacity — inflow design flood control (§257.82(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner or operator of an existing or new CCR surface impoundment, legacy CCR surface impoundment, or any lateral expansion must design, construct, operate, and maintain an inflow design flood control system as specified in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection requirements for CCR surface impoundments (§257.83(a) & (b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: All CCR surface impoundments, including legacy and any lateral expansion, must be examined by a qualified person as specified; if subject to periodic structural stability assessment requirements under §257.73(d) or §257.74(d), the CCR unit must additionally be inspected periodically by a qualified professional engineer to ensure design, construction, operation, and maintenance are consistent with recognized and generally accepted good engineering standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The periodic PE inspection must, at a minimum, include the items specified in the regulation (inspection scope details referenced in §257.83).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of groundwater monitoring and corrective action (§257.90(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All CCR units are subject to the groundwater monitoring and corrective action requirements under §§257.90 through 257.98, except as provided in paragraph (g) of §257.90.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial groundwater monitoring timeframes for existing CCR landfills and surface impoundments (§257.90(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than October 17, 2017, owner/operator must: (i) install the groundwater monitoring system as required by §257.91; (ii) develop the groundwater sampling and analysis program including selection of statistical procedures as required by §257.93; (iii) initiate the detection monitoring program obtaining a minimum of eight independent samples for each background and downgradient well as required by §257.94(b); and (iv) begin evaluating groundwater monitoring data for statistically significant increases over background levels for constituents listed in appendix III as required by §257.94.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial groundwater monitoring timeframes for new CCR landfills/surface impoundments (§257.90(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to initial receipt of CCR, owner/operator must be in compliance with groundwater monitoring requirements to install monitoring system and develop sampling/analysis program (including statistical procedures), and must initiate the detection monitoring program obtaining a minimum of eight independent samples for each background well as required by §257.94(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater monitoring timeframes for CCR management units (§257.90(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than May 8, 2028, owner/operator of CCR management unit must: (i) install groundwater monitoring system as required by §257.91; (ii) develop sampling and analysis program including statistical procedures as required by §257.93; (iii) initiate detection monitoring obtaining a minimum of eight independent samples for each background and downgradient well as required by §257.94(b); (iv) begin evaluating data for statistically significant increases over background for constituents in appendix III as required by §257.94; and (v) begin evaluating data for statistically significant levels over groundwater protection standards for constituents in appendix IV as required by §257.95.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing requirement to conduct groundwater monitoring and corrective action (§257.90(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a groundwater monitoring system and groundwater monitoring program has been established, the owner/operator must conduct groundwater monitoring and, if necessary, corrective action throughout the active life and post-closure care period of the CCR unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response obligations for a release from a CCR unit (§257.90(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a release from a CCR unit, the owner/operator must immediately take all necessary measures to control the source(s) of releases to reduce or eliminate, to the maximum extent feasible, further releases of contaminants into the environment and must comply with all applicable requirements in §§257.96, 257.97, and 257.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action report content and timing (§257.90(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must prepare an annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action report by specified dates (varies by unit type); the report must be placed in operating record and, for the preceding calendar year, document status of program, summarize key actions, describe problems and resolutions, and project upcoming activities. At minimum include: (1) map/aerial/diagram of CCR unit and all background/downgradient wells with IDs; (2) identification and narrative for wells installed/decommissioned; (3) summary of monitoring data including number of samples, dates, and program type; (4) narrative of any transition between monitoring programs including date/circumstances and constituents detected; (5) other info required by §§257.90–257.98; and (6) an overview section specifying program status at start/end of reporting period, details on statistically significant increases (appendix III) and levels above groundwater protection standards (appendix IV) with dates for assessment initiation, public meetings, remedy selection and remedial activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner/operator is deemed to have prepared the annual report when placed in the facility's operating record per §257.105(h)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping, notification, and internet requirements for groundwater monitoring (§257.90(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must comply with recordkeeping requirements in §257.105(h), notification requirements in §257.106(h), and internet requirements in §257.107(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of groundwater monitoring requirements (no-migration demonstration) (§257.90(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating State Director or EPA may suspend groundwater monitoring requirements for up to ten years if owner/operator provides written documentation demonstrating there is no potential for migration of constituents listed in appendices III and IV to the uppermost aquifer during active life and post-closure, certified by a qualified professional engineer and approved by the State Director or EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstration must be based on site-specific field-collected measurements/sampling/analysis of processes affecting contaminant fate and transport including aquifer characteristics (hydraulic conductivity, gradient, porosity, thickness, saturation, stratigraphy, fracturing, heterogeneity, discharge/recharge areas), waste characteristics, climatic conditions, leachate characteristics, and engineered controls evaluated under design and failure conditions; contaminant fate and transport predictions must maximize migration and consider human health/environmental impacts. Suspension may be renewed in additional ten-year periods with updated documentation and P.E. certification; renewal documentation must be submitted one year before expiration; if suspended period expires or not approved, owner must begin monitoring within 90 days; place each completed demonstration in operating record and include any approved no-migration demonstration in annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment monitoring program sampling requirements (§257.95(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 days of triggering an assessment monitoring program, and annually thereafter: (i) except as provided (ii), owner/operator must sample and analyze groundwater for all constituents listed in appendix IV; (ii) owner/operator of a CCR management unit must sample and analyze for appendix IV constituents no later than May 8, 2028. The number of samples collected/analyzed for each well during each event must be consistent with §257.93(e) and at least one sample from each well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and alternative timeframe eligibility for inactive CCR surface impoundments (§257.100(a) & (e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Inactive CCR surface impoundments are subject to all requirements applicable to existing CCR surface impoundments (with specified exceptions for certain active non-fuel generators); an inactive impoundment is eligible for alternative timeframes if the owner/operator completed by specified deadlines the actions in (e)(1)(i)-(iii): (i) prepared and placed notification of intent to initiate closure in operating record by Dec 17, 2015; (ii) provided notification to State Director/Tribal authority by Jan 19, 2016; and (iii) placed the notification on CCR website by Jan 19, 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these actions were completed by the deadlines, owner/operator may follow alternative timeframes set out in paragraphs (e)(2)-(6); otherwise closure requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location restriction demonstrations for inactive CCR surface impoundments (§257.100(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 16, 2020, owner/operator of an inactive CCR surface impoundment must complete demonstrations for placement above the uppermost aquifer (§257.60(a)-(c)(3)), wetlands (§257.61(a)-(c)(3)), fault areas (§257.62(a)-(c)(3)), seismic impact zones (§257.63(a)-(c)(3)), and unstable areas (§257.64(a)-(d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to demonstrate compliance with these requirements subjects the owner/operator to closure requirements of §257.101(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design criteria deadlines for inactive CCR surface impoundments (§257.100(e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must meet specified design documentation deadlines: (i) by Apr 17, 2018 document liner type per §257.71(a)-(b); (ii) by Jun 16, 2017 place permanent identification marker as per §257.73(a)(1); (iii) by Oct 16, 2018 prepare and maintain an Emergency Action Plan per §257.73(a)(3); (iv) by Apr 17, 2018 compile history of construction per §257.73(b)-(c); (v) by Apr 17, 2018 complete initial hazard potential classification, structural stability, and safety factor assessments per §257.73 provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating criteria deadlines for inactive CCR surface impoundments (§257.100(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must meet operating task deadlines: (i) by Apr 18, 2017 prepare initial CCR fugitive dust control plan per §257.80(b); (ii) by Apr 17, 2018 prepare initial inflow design flood control system plan per §257.82(c); (iii) by Apr 18, 2017 initiate inspections by a qualified person per §257.83(a); (iv) by Jul 19, 2017 complete initial annual inspection by a qualified professional engineer per §257.83(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater monitoring and corrective action timeframes for inactive CCR surface impoundments (§257.100(e)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must: (i) by Apr 17, 2019 comply with groundwater monitoring requirements set forth in §§257.90(b) and 257.94(b); and (ii) by Aug 1, 2019 prepare the initial groundwater monitoring and corrective action report as set forth in §257.90(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure and post-closure care deadlines for inactive CCR surface impoundments (§257.100(e)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must: (i) by Apr 17, 2018 prepare an initial written closure plan as per §257.102(b); and (ii) by Apr 17, 2018 prepare an initial written post-closure care plan as per §257.104(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy CCR surface impoundment applicability report and contents (§257.100(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must prepare an applicability report for each legacy impoundment no later than Nov 8, 2024 and place it in the facility operating record per §257.105(k)(1). At minimum the report must contain: (A) name and address of person(s) owning and operating unit with business phone/email; (B) name associated with the legacy impoundment; (C) identifying information including facility figure, unit location, facility address, latitude/longitude; (D) identification number if assigned by the state; (E) description of current site conditions including current use of inactive facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner/operator must certify the applicability report under penalty of law with the standard certification statement and notify the Agency of establishment of facility CCR website and applicability of rule via procedures in §257.107(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension for field investigation to determine presence of CCR and liquids (§257.100(f)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the applicability report deadline, an owner/operator may secure additional time solely to determine through a field investigation whether the unit contains both CCR and liquids; the amount of additional time is limited as specified in the regulation.
